title: Zone culling
description: Draw only what can be seen from where the camera stands: three.js frustum-culls but never occlusion-culls, so indoors it draws every room behind the walls. Give it the level's zone boxes and which zones each one sees (through doors, glass, windows); it buckets every top-level object into the smallest zone that wholly contains it and hides the zones you can't see. It hides through render layers, never `visible`, so the game keeps full control of what it shows and hides. Walls and floors on zone borders stay drawn, groups across a border are split, and moving things, skinned characters and lights are never hidden. userData.zone names the zone of an InstancedMesh. Cut Heartland Inn's lobby from 1,180 to 823 draw calls. Also the skeleton of a multi-level game: zones plus what each sees.
author: the internet slop warehouse

exports.name: attach
exports.signature: attach(scene, { zones, sees, margin }) → { update(eye), refresh(obj), zoneAt(eye), stats() }
exports.does: buckets the scene by zone; update(camera.position) each frame shows only the zones seen from there

options.name: zones
options.type: [{ name | id, x0, x1, y0, y1, z0, z1 }]
options.does: zone boxes in world metres; overlapping is fine, the smallest wins

options.name: sees
options.does: what each zone can see; 'outside' is no zone; a zone missing here sees everything

options.name: margin
options.does: how far inside a zone's box an object must sit to belong to it, metres
